candidates.name: Ovarian Neoplasm
support_spans: Although tumor markers were normal, the imaging findings were concerning for an ovarian neoplasm.
A staging laparotomy with surgical excision was planned, with a provisional diagnosis of a malignant ovarian tumor in the setting of uterine fibroids and unilateral lymphedema.
candidates.why: The patient's presentation with a large adnexal mass and imaging findings of a solid-cystic lesion in the abdominopelvic region are consistent with an ovarian neoplasm.

candidates.name: Meigs Syndrome
support_spans: a firm, non-tender, mobile mass measuring approximately 12 cm × 10 cm in the right lower quadrant; bimanual pelvic examination confirmed a right adnexal mass.
Transvaginal ultrasound showed multiple uterine fibroids and a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa.
candidates.why: The patient's presentation with a large adnexal mass and ascites is consistent with Meigs Syndrome, although the absence of ascites in the provided vignette makes this diagnosis less likely.

candidates.why: The patient's presentation with a large adnexal mass and the imaging findings of a solid-cystic lesion are consistent with an ovarian fibroma, especially given the association with unilateral lymphedema.

a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion

candidates.name: Ovarian cystadenoma
support_spans: a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion measuring 16.1 × 7.9 × 8.1 cm in the abdominopelvic region containing a 2.3 × 2.1 cm cystic component and a 5.8 × 5.7 cm solid component
candidates.why: The presence of a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion is more indicative of a benign ovarian tumor such as ovarian cystadenoma.

candidates.name: Ovarian fibroma
support_spans: a firm, non-tender, mobile mass measuring approximately 12 cm × 10 cm in the right lower quadrant
candidates.why: The description of the mass as firm and non-tender is consistent with ovarian fibroma, a type of benign ovarian tumor.

candidates.name: Meigs syndrome
support_spans: unilateral lymphedema
a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa
candidates.why: The combination of a large adnexal mass and unilateral lymphedema could be indicative of Meigs syndrome, a rare condition characterized by an ovarian tumor, ascites, and pleural effusion, although the ascites and pleural effusion are not mentioned in this case.

selector.rationale: The presence of a firm, non-tender, mobile mass and a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa, along with the patient's overall clinical presentation, supports Ovarian Fibroma as the most likely diagnosis.
